summary: The client called because their bill was significantly higher than usual this month and they were unsure why. The agent reviewed the account and identified an end-of-cycle promotional discount as a primary cause of the increase. They removed the installation fee and credited the customer’s account, clarifying that future bills will reflect the standard rate. Finally, the client expressed gratitude for the resolution.

response_times.client_text: My bill is a lot higher than usual this month and I don't understand why.
response_times.agent_text: I understand, an unexpected jump is worrying. Let me go through the bill with you line by line.
First, can I confirm the name and address on the account for security?
Thank you, John. I have the bill in front of me now.
The first thing I see is that a promotional discount ended this cycle, and that's most of the increase.

response_times.client_text: Ah, I forgot about the promo.
response_times.agent_text: That's completely normal. There's also a one-off installation fee I want to check.

response_times.client_text: The installation was months ago though.
response_times.agent_text: You're right, and it should have been billed back then. Billing it now is our error.
Yes, I'll remove that fee and credit your account for it today.
To be clear, going forward your bill will be the standard rate now the promo has ended.
Would you like me to look at current offers so you can keep the price down?
I've applied a loyalty discount for six months. You'll see it next cycle. Anything else?
